claims.text: The rider's claim is proven on this trip's own trace: the GPS polyline runs 31.2 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events against a booked optimal of 24.0 km, an excess of 7.2 km and 30.0% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass — the excess exceeds 20% of optimal and exceeds 0.8 km absolute — so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. Under POL-RD-01 the governing field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km, and the trace figure is the one cited here.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and discharges it: the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02810 and the trace's first fix at 2026-08-20T21:09:44+08:00 matches the trip_record.started_at exactly, so the artifacts describe the same trip; and the excess of 7.2 km / 30.0% meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on a trace that is unimpaired. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause.

The driver's only explanation is 'AYE closed, I had to divert.' That is an uncited traffic assertion. POL-RD-13 requires an external-traffic excuse to be tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, and POL-RD-08 provides that a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden. The driver names no advisory identifier, so the assertion carries no weight and the deviation stands at the measured figure.

Even taken at its highest, the driver's closure excuse cannot reach the measured excess. The advisory on file (ADV-20260820-069, AYE towards Tuas after Clementi Ave 6) gives a shortest lawful alternative of 26.0 km against a booked optimal of 24.0 km, so the POL-RD-03 cap on justified excess is min(7.2, 1.30 x (26.0 - 24.0) + 1.00) = min(7.2, 3.60) = 3.60 km. The remaining 3.6 km of excess is not exonerated and is refundable under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route.

The trace never enters the advisory's own area: the derived advisory_area block records zero fixes inside the advisory geometry and a minimum distance of 1699.49 m from it. POL-RD-03(c) requires an actual route that leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after; a trace that never comes within 1.7 km of the closed segment cannot satisfy that limb, so the exoneration fails on its own terms as well as on the cap.

No rider-requested detour can excuse any of this distance. The chat log for TRP-02810 carries zero messages, so there is no rider instruction, no waypoint_hint and no named road; POL-RD-04 is unavailable on the record and no distance is excluded on that ground. The driver's own counterparty statement asserts a closure, not a rider request.

No relocation clause applies either: trip_record.pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and the booked optimal of 24.0 km stands as the baseline. The trip is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and solo_optimal_distance_km is not in play.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal route. Adjusted optimal distance = 24.0 + 3.60 = 27.60 km; adjusted duration = 32.0 x (27.60 / 24.0) = 36.8 min. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 27.60 + 0.28 x 36.8) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = 3.80 + 20.70 + 10.304 + 0.80 = 35.604. Refund = charged_total 39.40 - 35.604 = 3.796, rounded up to SGD 3.80. The surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which is 1.0.

The refund is not de minimis: SGD 3.80 exceeds the SGD 0.50 floor in POL-RD-02, so NO_ACTION is not available on that ground. It is also far below the 90% full-refund share of charged_total, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND, not FULL_REFUND.

No ERP or surcharge correction is due. The fare_breakdown carries zero ERP lines and zero airport surcharge, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to add and nothing to subtract; in particular the off-route ERP pass-through correction in POL-RD-09(2) is nil because no gantry was charged at all.

The driver's profile does not establish a repeat-deviation pattern under POL-RD-06: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 196, so neither the 3-or-more limb nor the 0.05 ratio limb is met. The POL-RD-06(b) FULL_REFUND uplift is therefore unavailable and the remedy stays at the POL-RD-02 partial. I note for completeness that prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and is not the field POL-RD-06 names.

The rider's profile does not trigger the POL-RD-08 corroboration overlay: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the 4-or-more threshold, so no extra corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required and the claim stands on the trace alone.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 245 fixes at a 10 s sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 s, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) are not engaged, no independent corroboration is required, and POL-RD-10(3) does not fire. The admissibility pre-pass likewise tags EV-GPS-02810 COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across all three artifacts, the trace is unimpaired, no timestamps run backwards or disagree by more than 10 minutes, the refund of SGD 3.80 is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total, and every charge line has a counterpart in the record. The case can be decided on the money.

I concede one point against my side: the driver's assertion of an AYE closure is not fabricated — a real LTA advisory for the AYE towards Tuas after Clementi Ave 6 was in force from 20:39:44 to 22:15:24 on the trip date and overlaps the trip window by 70.7 minutes. That is why the POL-RD-03 cap of 3.60 km of justified excess is allowed rather than zero. It does not carry the remaining 3.6 km, because the trace never enters the advisory area and the cap is a cap.

The driver names no evidence ID for any advisory, and the assertion therefore carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

The chat log for this trip contains zero messages. There is no rider instruction of any kind, so POL-RD-04 cannot be invoked: no message from the rider, no timestamp, no waypoint_hint. The rider-requested-detour exoneration is unavailable on the record.

The trip record shows no amendment to pickup or dropoff: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-05 cannot be run and the booked 24.0 km optimal stands as the baseline.
The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-12 does not apply and the matched-itinerary baseline is not in play.

The GPS trace is clean for policy purposes: 245 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0. It does not meet any of POL-RD-07(a) to (c), so the deviation may be established on the trace alone and no independent corroboration is required.

The rider has discharged the POL-RD-08 burden: the trip identifier TRP-02810 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and the excess of 7.2 km meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden shifts to the driver, who has pointed to no specific artifact and no specific clause.

The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs. Charged total is SGD 39.40. The recomputed fare on the booked optimal route is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 24.0 + 0.28 x 32.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 31.56. The refund is 39.40 - 31.56 = 7.84, rounded up to SGD 7.85. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and below 90% of charged_total, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND.

The fare breakdown carries zero ERP lines and zero tolls, so there is no off-route ERP pass-through to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure and no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4). The refund is the distance-and-time figure alone.

The driver's profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 and completed_trips_90d of 196. That is below the POL-RD-06 threshold of 3 flags, and 0/196 is below the 0.05 ratio. No repeat-deviation pattern is established and no POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral follows. I concede this point.

The rider's profile shows deviation_claims_60d of 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0. That is below the POL-RD-08 threshold of 4 claims, so no additional corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required for this claim.

The traffic advisory on file (ADV-20260820-069) is a HIGH-severity vehicle fire on the AYE towards Tuas, active 20:39:44 to 22:15:24, overlapping the trip window. But the derived advisory-area test shows the trace enters the advisory's area on zero fixes, with a minimum distance of 1699.5 m. The driver's route never went near the closed segment, so POL-RD-03(c) is not satisfied and the advisory does not exonerate the deviation.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. You were billed SGD 39.40 (fare breakdown EV-FARE-02810) for a trip the GPS trace EV-GPS-02810 records at 31.2 km against a booked optimal of 24.0 km (trip record EV-TRIP-02810). Under POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs the distance, and it shows an excess of 7.2 km, 30.0% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass (above 4.8 km and above 0.8 km), so a deviation is established. The deviation is not MATERIAL (30% is under 50% and 7.2 km is under 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged; in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 196 completed trips in 90 days, so there is no repeat-pattern uplift and no conduct referral. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags was mentioned only to say it is not the field POL-RD-06 names; it is context-only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used as a ground.

The driver's message 'AYE closed, I had to divert' cites no evidence ID and carries no weight by itself under POL-RD-08. The record does, however, hold the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-02810-01 (weight 1.0): it names the AYE towards Tuas after Clementi Ave 6, a segment the booked optimal route traverses, and was in force 20:39:44–22:15:24, overlapping the trip window (21:09:44–21:50:24) by 70.7 minutes. The trace itself is unimpaired (245 fixes, 10 s interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps, max gap 0 s), so POL-RD-07 does not engage and no independent corroboration is needed. On the actual route the trace stays entirely clear of the closed stretch (0 fixes inside the advisory geometry, minimum approach 1,699.5 m); because the optimal route runs through that stretch, a route that avoids it necessarily left the optimal corridor around the affected segment and rejoined it, so POL-RD-03(c) is met. I therefore did not accept the argument, made on both sides, that POL-RD-03 fails outright because the trace never enters the advisory's area: avoiding the closed area is what a diversion looks like, and the derived advisory-area figure was one to weigh, not one that decides by itself.

Exoneration under POL-RD-03 is capped: min(7.2, 1.30 x (26.0 - 24.0) + 1.00) = 3.60 km. The closure explains 3.60 km of the 7.2 km excess and no more; the remaining 3.6 km is refundable. The closure-adjusted optimal is 24.0 + 3.60 = 27.60 km, with duration 32.0 x (27.60 / 24.0) = 36.8 min.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. The fare model is METERED and the surge multiplier of 1.0 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (EV-FARE-02810). recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 27.60 + 0.28 x 36.8) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = 35.604. charged_total = 39.40. refund = 39.40 - 35.604 = 3.796, rounded up to SGD 3.80. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and 9.6% of the charged total, well below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a partial refund of SGD 3.80.

Other points raised are answered as follows. No rider-requested detour is available: the chat log EV-CHAT-02810 holds zero messages, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run and no distance is excluded on that ground. No pick-up or drop-off amendment exists (both timestamps null and the amended optimal distance null), so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and the booked 24.0 km baseline stands. The vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply. POL-RD-09 adds nothing: the fare breakdown carries no ERP lines and no airport surcharge, so there is no pass-through correction and no billing-integrity finding. The rider's profile does not trigger the POL-RD-08 corroboration overlay (deviation_claims_60d is 1, below 4). No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across trip record, trace and fare breakdown, the trace is unimpaired, the timestamps agree, the refund is far below SGD 150.00 and below the charged total, and every charge line has a counterpart in the record.

SGD 3.80 is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so it will be executed on issue. Each party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

To both of you. I decided this on the trip record EV-TRIP-02810, the GPS trace EV-GPS-02810, the fare breakdown EV-FARE-02810 and the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-02810-01. Every artifact I rely on is admitted at full weight 1.00, so nothing is discounted under POL-GEN-02.

1) The deviation is real. The trace runs 31.2 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events against a booked optimal of 24.0 km — an excess of 7.2 km, or 30.0% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (over 20% and over 0.8 km), and the trace figure governs over the rounded trip-record copy. The trace is clean for POL-RD-07 purposes (245 fixes, 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps), so no independent corroboration is required and POL-RD-10(3) does not fire.

2) The driver's diversion is partly explained, and I accept it to the extent POL-RD-03 allows. ruling.explanation:
To both parties.

THE DEVIATION. Trip TRP-02810 ran from Northpoint City to Blk 503 Bishan St 11 on 20 August 2026 against a booked optimal of 24.0 km. The GPS trace measures the route actually driven at 31.2 km — an excess of 7.2 km, or 30.0% of optimal. POL-RD-01 sets two tests and both pass (more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km absolute), so the deviation is established. I used the trace figure (gps_trace.trace_distance_km), which POL-RD-01 makes the governing measurement, not the trip record's rounded copy. Both advocates agree on this point.

THE CLOSURE. The driver's explanation — 'AYE closed, I had to divert' — is tested against the traffic advisory for this trip, and the bundle contains one: ADV-20260820-069, an LTA record of a vehicle fire closing all lanes of the Ayer Rajah Expressway towards Tuas after Clementi Ave 6, in force 20:39:44–22:15:24, covering the whole trip window (21:09:44–21:50:24) and intersecting the booked optimal route. POL-RD-03(a) and (b) are therefore satisfied. The assertion itself cited no advisory ID and, standing alone, would carry no weight under POL-RD-08; it is the advisory on the record, not the assertion, that carries the excuse.

For POL-RD-03(c) the question is whether the route actually driven left the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoined it after. The trace's closest approach to the closed segment is 1,699 m and no fix falls inside the advisory area: the vehicle went around the closure rather than through it. That is the signature limb (c) describes, so the excuse is not discarded. I reject the argument that exoneration fails outright because the trace never enters the advisory area — a trace that DID enter the closed area is what would defeat limb (c).

But exoneration is capped, and the cap is where the excuse stops. The shortest lawful alternative was 26.0 km against the 24.0 km optimal, so the justified excess is min(7.2, 1.30 × (26.0 − 24.0) + 1.00) = min(7.2, 3.60) = 3.60 km. Only 3.60 km of the 7.2 km is excused; the remaining 3.6 km is charged to the driver and refunded to the rider.

THE REFUND. The fare model is metered, so POL-RD-02 runs, and because POL-RD-03 excuses part of the excess it runs against the closure-adjusted optimal route: 24.0 + 3.60 = 27.60 km, with duration 32.0 × (27.60 / 24.0) = 36.8 minutes. The surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and is 1.0.
- Charged total: SGD 39.40.
- Recomputed fare: (3.80 + 0.75 × 27.60 + 0.28 × 36.8) × 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 35.604.
- Refund: 39.40 − 35.604 = SGD 3.796, rounded up to SGD 3.80.

The claim that the refund should be computed against the booked 24.0 km optimal and come to SGD 7.85 is rejected: it treats the closure as exonerating nothing, contrary to the advisory in the record. SGD 3.80 is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and far below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a partial refund of SGD 3.80.

EVERYTHING ELSE. There is no rider-requested detour to exclude — the chat log for TRP-02810 carries zero messages — and no pickup or dropoff amendment; the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL and solo_optimal_distance_km is not in play. POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 therefore give nothing. No ERP or toll line was charged, so POL-RD-09 adds no pass-through correction and no billing-integrity referral arises. The driver's profile shows no repeat-deviation pattern under POL-RD-06 (deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 196), so the FULL_REFUND uplift and the conduct referral do not fire; the rider's profile shows 1 deviation claim in 60 days, below the POL-RD-08 threshold, so no corroboration beyond the trace is required. Only the profile fields POL-GEN-01 names as citable were used; no reputation field decided anything. The trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 (245 fixes, 10-second interval, no gaps, no jumps) and no POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across trip record, trace and fare breakdown, no timestamps disagree, and every charge line has a counterpart in the record.

OUTCOME. Partial refund of SGD 3.80 to the rider; no driver compensation and no referrals. The amount is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so it is executed on issue. Confidence 0.85. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.
